$comment: Animation state map for the pixel-coder placeholder pet. THIS FILE IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for animation geometry: `pnpm generate` turns it into the renderer's CSS keyframes and into the AnimationState TypeScript union. Never hand-write a row offset, frame count or duration anywhere else. Geometry matches openpets' defaultPetSprite exactly.

failed.note: 8 declared frames but only 6 distinct: the last three repeat, which is what holds the final slumped pose. Do NOT 'optimise' this to 6 frames — that changes the timing and loses the beat.

drink.note: Reclaimed from the old `waiting` state, which was byte-identical to row 0 and so was never an animation at all. Art is still pending: until it is drawn this plays the idle frames, which keeps the water-reminder trigger path complete and testable today.

running.note: In-place busy/working loop, NOT locomotion — locomotion is running-left/running-right. Never wire this to movement.

sleep.note: The idle frames re-timed very slow, paired with a pure-CSS 'Z' overlay. Ships with no new art at all; two states sharing one row is deliberate and allowed.

aliases.$comment: Substitutions for states the behaviour spec needs but the art does not contain yet. The reactionMap deliberately keeps naming the state it *wants*, so when the art lands the only change is deleting the alias entry — no code edits, no mapping edits. An alias target must be a real declared state; the generator enforces that.

plannedNewStates.$comment: Still absent from the sheet. Requires extending it to 12 rows (1536x2496).

stretch.note: Aliased to `jumping` until drawn — see the `aliases` block.

freeCells.$comment: Unused (fully transparent) cells available for new frames without resizing the sheet.

reactionMap.$comment: trigger -> animation state. Keep this indirection so a new trigger is a mapping entry rather than renderer work. A value may name a state or an alias.
